chapter: Wingy Manone and Bix in Chicago (retyped)
title: The 1942 Decca date at nine in the morning
summary: Hodes tells how a fan's father got him a Decca date through Dave Kapp. The only slot offered was 9 a.m., and the engineers set up the studio badly. He says it was still one of his best dates.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And you don't drag yourself like that. And a good example of that was getting up at 9:00 in the morning, because that's the only time Decca would give us to make a date in 1942.
Oh, that was the first date under your label?
Yeah, That was the first date under your name? "Georgia Camp Meeting"

Right. And I got the date because I had a fan whose father knew Dave Kapp very well. They played cards together, and so he talked to Dave Kapp about getting me a date. And Dave Kapp took my "From the Gutter" Selections, we got a single record that I made for Bob Thiele at the time that he was into this kind of thing.

And he took it home with him and played it. And asked his black maid, did that do anything for her, and she says, yeah, that's great. And so I got a date. Otherwise, I wouldn't have got the date. At 9:00 in the morning they gave us a date.

Now, imagine, everybody stayed up, because nobody -- if we worked til 4:00, nobody thought of going home and by the time you go to bed and everything it gets to be 6:00, then you got to get up at 8:00 to get to the studio, and you said to heck with it. So you stayed up. But it was different. Everybody showed up grumpy, growly, but they showed up and they showed up to play. And they played.

Now, although some of us never talked to each other when we left that place, we were spoilsports. And mostly because the engineers, again, like we were talking, set up to suit themselves. They didn't set up to suit us. They muffled the drums and put them over there in the corner, put the piano in another corner, put Murphy -- I think he was playing bass, in another corner, put Eddie Condom somewhere else. We just weren't together like we would be on a job.
And we thought it was a terrible thing to do. But it turned out that it was one of the best dates we ever made, we ever made at that time.
